    Priorities

    What matters to you? Your sliders change your overall score everywhere on the page. Everyone you compare with sets their own, so you can see where your priorities differ.

    How the score works

    • Walking time, not distance. A supermarket 3 minutes away counts fully, at 10 minutes about a third, and past 20 minutes not at all. Parks, sport and culture get more slack: Englischer Garten 10 minutes away still counts 85%.
    • Choice counts too. For cafés, restaurants, bars and shops, the 2nd, 3rd and 10th option add to the score, so a street with twelve cafés beats a street with one.
    • Transit counts lines. Sendlinger Tor (six U-Bahn lines) beats a single-line stop. U- and S-Bahn weigh most, then tram, then bus.
    • Street life counts every shop, café, bar and service within 500 m. It's the density that makes a street feel like a city.
    • Overall is the average of the 13 categories, weighted by each person's priorities.
    • Real walking routes. Every distance follows actual streets, paths, steps and bridges at 4.8 km/h, so the Isar, rail tracks, the Mittlerer Ring and fenced-off areas count as the barriers they are. On the map, the highlighted streets show how far you get in 5, 10 and 15 minutes from the selected spot.
    • Street life is the one count done as the crow flies, since it measures how dense the area around you is.
    • Data: OpenStreetMap. Shops open and close, and some may be missing.
